text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (also called LFP) is the better choice.** Nearly every current power station uses it, and the sources I found agree on why.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LiFePO4 stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles. The NMC models in these sources are rated for about 500-1,000 (one guide says up to 2,000). Used daily, that's roughly 8+ years versus under 2 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells peaked at lower temperatures and failed less violently. One test had LFP at about 259°C versus 731°C for NMC. LFP isn't fireproof, and one study found it reached runaway earlier in overcharge. The advantage is milder failure, which matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Cost per cycle:** LFP is cheaper per rated cycle. One retailer-guide dataset shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per pound, but the gap mostly shrinks in finished stations. Estimates range from about 10% to 30% depending on the source. One LFP station (Anker SOLIX C1000) is actually lighter per Wh than an NMC Goal Zero Yeti 1000 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare the specific models rather than assuming.

**Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd think. Most stations of either type won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual for the specific unit ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Quick guide**
- **Daily or frequent use, such as a van, off-grid setup, or a UPS:** LiFePO4.
- **Home backup used a few times a year:** Either works, since calendar aging will matter more than cycles. LiFePO4 is still the safer default at similar prices.
- **Weight-critical and rarely used:** Compare specific models. NMC may be lighter.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.

If you buy NMC, make sure the price reflects it. Also check the spec page for the chemistry, since a few units don't state it.

**Example LiFePO4 pick:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating, a 5-year warranty, and no expansion. It suits fridge-and-router backup for a day or two. It lists at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the source tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-24. The store's checkout has the final word on price ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)). That is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. It's one example, not a verdict that it's the best option for you.
